name: Ton Diepeveen - Projet de décision du Conseil
title: RECOMMENDATION on the draft Council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the Union, of the Protocol (2025–2029) on the implementation of the Fisheries Partnership Agreement between the Republic of Côte d’Ivoire and the European Community
part_text:
The European Parliament agrees to a new four-year fishing deal between the European Union and Côte d'Ivoire, a country in West Africa. The deal lets up to 32 EU boats, mainly from Spain, Portugal and France, catch tuna in Côte d'Ivoire's waters. In return, the EU pays €740,000 a year: €305,000 for fishing rights and €435,000 to help Côte d'Ivoire manage its fisheries, fight illegal fishing and support coastal communities. Parliament's committees back the deal and ask for better scrutiny of how the money is used.

- What changes: EU boats regain access to Côte d'Ivoire's waters for tuna fishing until 2029, under a new four-year deal.
- Who it affects: EU fishing crews, mainly Spanish, Portuguese and French, and people in Côte d'Ivoire who depend on fishing jobs and fish as food.
- What happens next: Parliament's formal consent lets the deal be concluded and start applying; the EU budget must release the money.
